name: v2.13.10 — ai-seo (2.11.0 → 2.12.0): agent readiness adds a skill file for your product: a public S…
body:
- **ai-seo** (2.11.0 → 2.12.0): agent readiness adds **a skill file for your product**: a public `SKILL.md` that uses the context the buyer's agent already has to propose setup choices, quotes published pricing, and returns a prefilled checkout or signup URL (price recomputed on the server, parameters validated, agent orders tagged). Agent-only offers are fine when stated as information; forced upsells and instructions tuned to always push an offer are called out as prompt injection. Prompted by Ilias Ism's post on LinkDR's SKILL.md.
- **video** (2.3.0 → 2.4.0): new reference **code-rendered product films**: every frame a pure function of time over real DOM snapshots of a seeded app, a private video repo with one worktree per video, claims checked against source with docs-vs-UI discrepancies logged, a running `AGENTS.md` of taste rules, multi-take TTS with a judge, beat-grid music cuts and loudness targets, contact-sheet review (judge models as hints only), and hero video measurement by `video_id`. Adapted from Elie Steinbock's Inbox Zero write-up.
- **ab-testing** (2.0.3 → 2.0.4): opt-in elements such as a hero video underpower tests on overall conversion; use a triggered analysis or compare versions on viewer metrics.
- **Tools**: SavvyCal is now listed as MCP-enabled (official remote server with OAuth), and its v1 API guide and CLI are corrected against the OpenAPI spec (#918, contributed by Derrick Reimer and Jesse Leite of SavvyCal).

## Skill ZIP assets

Complete source catalog: 52 skills.
Claude web target: 52 skills with reviewed short descriptions.
Perplexity Computer target: 52 skills.

Choose `<name>-claude-web.zip` for the documented single-folder web upload format.
Choose `<name>-perplexity.zip` for Perplexity Computer (SKILL.md at the archive root).
Source ZIPs retain original metadata; they are not substitutes for omitted web ZIPs.
Live client upload, account limits, and invocation behavior have not been verified.

Web omissions (also recorded in `claude-web-manifest.json`):
- None.

name: v0.6.9
body:
**ripwire 0.6.9: better answers to the questions agents ask (a `--path` that prints the bodies it names, call chains and callers that earlier builds left out), and more hedged or declined calls instead of confident wrong ones.** This release collects twelve merged batches of reviewed changes (pull requests #424 to #463). The next section shows real before and after output; section 1 is about honesty (hedged or declined calls, floors named, the bodies `--path` prints); section 2 is the new `--defs` verb and `Owner.name` selectors; section 3 is language specifics and callers for error-shaped `--for` questions. Every item is an entry in the changelog, which states what it was measured on and what it does not show; statements here are in-sample, and this page makes no comparison with any other tool.

## Better answers to the questions agents ask
Each line is a question from the sets we developed ripwire against (in-sample, not held out), run with the same command on 0.6.8 and 0.6.9; sizes are the whole answer.
Eight of these nine are questions whose answer spans several files or runs through indirection: an interface or trait call, a message queue, a renamed import.

**Across files: call chains, callers and the code on the route**
- **TypeScript (hono): how does `fetch` reach `compose`?** 0.6.8 named the hops and printed no code (1,005 B). 0.6.9 also prints the middle hop's body, where the `compose( … )` call sits, and names each method's class (`Hono.#dispatch`; 3,973 B).
- **C (htop): `ScreenManager_run` to `LinuxMachine_scanCPUTime`.** The hedged route was named without its code; now the three bodies come with it (3,444 to 10,699 B).
- **Go (terraform): the call chain from `Context.Plan` to `Graph.walk`.** 0.6.8 printed no chain (22,049 B). 0.6.9 appends the six-hop chain, `Context.PlanAndEval`, `plan`, `planWalk`, `walk`, `Graph.Walk`, `Graph.walk` (24,389 B).
- **Rust (nushell): the call chain from `main` to `eval_block_with_early_return` when a script file runs.** 0.6.8 printed no chain (23,599 B). 0.6.9 appends the five-hop chain through `run_file` (28,310 B).
- **Go (cockroach): which non-test functions call `NewReplicaEvalContext`?** 0.6.8 named none of the four callers (21,812 B). 0.6.9 appends a callers answer that names all four, with their call lines (24,928 B).

**Through indirection: dispatch, message queues, renamed imports**
- **Python (textual): how does `post_message` reach the `on_*` handlers?** 0.6.8 said "not reached", with no route (3,480 B). 0.6.9 prints a route marked as a hedge (`proven="0"`) through the message queue to `_dispatch_message`, with the four bodies (13,973 B).
- **Rust (mdbook): what does `execute_build_process` call?** A call on a `&dyn Renderer` was bound by name to the test stub `TestRenderer` in the same file (`render`, `name`; 1,526 B). Now it is declined and says what could run: `<dc n="render" l="207" cands="5" via="declined" gate="iface"/>`, five renderers (2,000 B).
- **Python (cpython): who calls `re.sub`?** Calls written `from re import sub as re_sub` were not counted; now `TimeRE.pattern` and `LocaleTime.__calc_date_time` are (73 to 75 callers).

**Unused code**
- **Python (textual): which functions in `_segment_tools.py` have no caller?** 0.6.8 printed `count="0"` (1,025 B). 0.6.9 adds `<to n="align_lines">`, a function only tests call (1,374 B).

On the 163 questions we developed against, same command on both versions, graded against our answer key: **complete answers went from 112 to 129, partial from 38 to 31, missing from 13 to 3**; total bytes per complete answer went from 16,523 to 15,099 (all answers together are 5% larger). One answer moved from complete to partial (ninja-14): 0.6.8 reached it by guessing one of three implementations by name; 0.6.9 shows the route as a hedge instead. Proving which implementation runs is planned work. These are in-sample numbers, not a prediction for other code.

## Read this first
- Caches are rebuilt once. Every ingest cache and quality snapshot an earlier build wrote is refused and re-indexed on first run (parser version 259, cache version 46, quality-snapshot scheme 24).
- Scripts that read `n=`: a member row on `--callers`, `--callees`, `--impact`, `--path` and signature rows now prints its owner (`Pattern.match`, `Builder::Build` in C, C++ and Rust, `Task#execute` in Ruby); the spelling is one every symbol verb accepts, so a row can be pasted back. On a signature `<d>` row the owner folds into `n=` and `sc=` is dropped. `--json` keys, `<c>` callee rows, tail rows and the map are unchanged.
- A `file:LINE` selector that two definitions start on now refuses and lists each candidate on stderr, instead of binding the innermost one without saying so.
- `--dead-code` prints a new `<to>` row group after its `<d>` rows (library functions whose every indexed caller is test code); they are not in `count=`. `--affected` adds a separate hedged group (`via="class-new"`) after the proven rows.
- `--situ` and `--test-gate` start the caller walk from the changed symbols, not from every symbol of every changed file. A hunk that no function body fully holds sends its whole file back to the old behaviour.
- `--for` and `--path` answers gain elements and attributes (`<callers>`, `<graph_verb>`, `<ep>`, `<alts>`, `<bodies>`, `slots=`, `mem=`, `ctor_l=`, `stem="1"` on the map); each is documented in its changelog entry and in the answer's own legend. Environment switches that turn a new behaviour off are named in the entries (for example `RIPWIRE_NO_HOP_BODY=1`, `RIPWIRE_NO_CTOR_HOP=1`, `RIPWIRE_NO_MAP_STEM=1`).
- Contributors: a changelog entry is now one new file under `changelog.d/`, folded into `CHANGELOG.md` at release.

## 1. Honesty first: hedged or declined instead of confidently wrong
Each item says what changes for an agent reading the answer. These are in-sample statements: each changelog entry names the repositories and rows it was checked on and what it does not show.
- **A name match is labelled as one.** A by-name hedge to a free function or a JavaScript/TypeScript method now needs the caller's file to be, or import, the namesake's file; an override counts as a way in. Hedged hops (`via="name"`, `via="name-key"`, `via="queue"`, `via="slot"`) are never counted in `reaches=`, `reachable=` or `hops=`, so those counts hold proven rows only.
- **Fewer wrong edges, stated as unresolved.** A JavaScript/TypeScript call through a name written after its declaration (`Eng = Foo; new Eng()`) is `unresolved=`, not the declared class. A Rust `&dyn Trait` call never binds a same-file impl by name when the trait's implementor list is open. `Widget.run` no longer binds a class's method when an object literal named `Widget` has a `run` too; the spelling is refused instead. `this.f.m()` on a typed field never binds the caller's own `m`. A Kotlin trailing-lambda `let`, `run`, `with`, `apply` or `also` stays off a Java method of the same name (#438, @llvm-x86).
- **A floor is named instead of a confident zero.** A call through an interface-, trait- or abstract-typed receiver names the implementors that can run, and the interface carries `implementors_floor=` when the list cannot be complete. `--lego` stops listing an implementor whose own file imports its base from outside the tree. `--grep` says when a literal pattern reads as a regex (`pattern_meta=`) instead of answering `hits="0"`; `--whereis` stops labelling comment, prose and string lines `kind="def"`; a `file:LINE` selector that two definitions start on refuses and lists each candidate instead of binding the innermost one silently.
- **`--dead-code` and `--safe-delete` stop over-reporting.** `static` counts as internal linkage only in C, C++ and Objective-C, and Django and unittest hooks are not reported as dead code (#437, @llvm-x86; reported in #228 by @hnipps). New `<to>` rows list library functions only tests call, apart from `count=`.
- **`--path` prints the bodies that hold its answer.** A short `--path` prints the body of its middle hop (whole up to 4,000 bytes, then cut and said so). An unreached `--path` that names a route prints the bodies of that route's bridge rows and readers, marked `proven="0"`. It lists every reaching definition pair when a name has several, the other definitions of an endpoint whose pick is not provably unique (`<alts>`), prints first the pair whose owner you named, and says when it bound a test or fixture copy of a name (`from_test=`, `to_test=`).
- **Hedged hops compose.** `--impact` counts who reaches a hedged caller, folds a hub in the hedged ring into one row, and `--affected` adds tests that construct a reached class as a separate hedged group (`via="class-new"`).

## 2. `--defs` and `Owner.name` selectors
- **New verb: `--defs=NAME[,NAME…]`.** One call answers which definitions up to 16 names bind: each row has the owner-qualified name, kind, `file:line`, language, source or test, its callers (a floor), and `sel=`, a spelling that picks that definition alone, so the next call needs no guessing.
- **Rows name their owner.** A member row on `--callers`, `--callees`, `--impact`, `--path` and signature rows prints `Pattern.match`, `Builder::Build` (C, C++, Rust) or `Task#execute` (Ruby), and every such spelling can be pasted back as a selector.
- **Names resolve as the source spells them.** `Class.method` in TypeScript, `json.dump`, `batcheval.Put`, `ns::Outer::Inner::f` and `Hono.#dispatch` now resolve; a JavaScript/TypeScript method row names its class; a bare `module.exports = (…) => …` is a function named by its file. A bare name with several definitions is ordered the same way in every verb, and `--lsp` says when a name has several (#432, @mpapis).

## 3. Language specifics, and callers for error-shaped questions
- **Rust.** A receiver written as a type (`&Book`, `Box<T>`, a path, a struct field) proves that type's method. Functions stored in struct fields are joined to the `(x.f)( … )` calls through them, in `--callers`, `--callees` and `--for`. Files using an empty `+ use<>` bound no longer lose every impl owner.
- **Python.** A call through a renamed import (`from m import f as g`) reaches `m.f`, also when the module defines `__getattr__`. Annotated fields (`self.f: T | None`) and `mod.X( … )` constructors type a receiver. A posted message class names its handlers (`<handler_rule>` on `--path`, `via="name-key"`), and a queue `put` hands off to the `get` readers (`via="queue"`). `--for` shows how a shown definition is registered through a manifest entry point.
- **Go, C and C++.** A function stored in a struct field (a Go keyed element, field assignment or registrar argument; a C `.exec = cmd_split_window_exec`) is joined to the dispatcher that calls it.
- **JavaScript and TypeScript.** A method row names its class; `--uses` on a literal receiver no longer lists built-in member calls (#411, @lennix1337).
- **Error-shaped `--for`.** A `--for` task about an error (error, exception, panic, raise, throw, fail, crash, Traceback, or an error type written as one identifier) with no function named carries the same `<callers>` chain the name-exact route carries, marked `by="rank"`, for the narrow function it ranks in rows 1 to 3.
- **More of what a `--for` question points at.** It follows a one-line wrapper into the function it calls, names what the top method's class constructor calls (`ctor_calls=`), the functions a shown table initializer binds (`slots=`) and the members of a shown owner (`mem=`), lists the callers of a function it is about, and answers a task spelled as a graph question (`path from A to B`, `callers of X`) with that verb's answer, honouring `--token-budget`.
- **Contexts that changed.** `--situ` and `--test-gate` start from the changed symbols, not every symbol of every changed file (#423, @llvm-x86).

## Platforms and safety
- Windows: `--quality-delta=A..B` extracts its per-commit trees through stdin, so a drive-letter path no longer fails (#402, #422, @lennix1337); clang-cl PGO builds link and keep SLP vectorization in the final binary (#410, @lennix1337).
- The pattern screen that guards `--regex`, `--graph-query file()`, `--arch` path rules and `#match?` refuses an overlapping alternation under an unbounded quantifier, one group deeper than before (#397, @pt-act).
- Gates that timed out on slow runners were made cheaper, with no change to the product (macOS impact-partition and C++ localization gates, memguard and pargates arms, the Linux ASan alarm, #421). A test arm of the type-3 clone gate was renamed so the gate checks it (#431, @liziye627-design; part of the cleanup @s0undt3ch asked for in #305).

## Known floors
- Every `via="name"`, `via="name-key"`, `via="queue"` and `via="slot"` row is a hedge, not a proof: it is never counted in `reaches=`, `reachable=` or `hops=`, and the readers or candidates it lists are a floor.
- A single pathological regular-expression match remains unbounded on libstdc++, tracked as `regex-screen-multiquantifier`.
- Not joined: a Rust closure stored in a field, a method-call registrar (`r.set( f )`) and a function value inside a macro; Go interface values (Go interfaces are structural); C typedef'd function-pointer fields copied between structs.
- Kotlin: a parenthesised lambda (`s.let( { } )`) is not a trailing lambda, and a Java method called from Kotlin with a trailing lambda is dropped when its name is a scope-function name.
- Python: a package that only re-exports a function, or an import inside another function, keeps the earlier answer for a renamed import.
- In MCP `for`, a middle-hop body the answer already prints can print a second time, because that twin has no served-body set to compare (a known divergence, named in the changelog).

## Thanks
Code: @lennix1337 (#402, #410, #411, #422: Windows `--quality-delta`, clang-cl PGO builds, `--uses` on literal receivers), @llvm-x86 (#423 `--situ` and `--test-gate` from changed symbols; #437 Django and unittest hooks; #438 Kotlin scope functions), @mpapis (#432: one order for every multi-definition name answer, and `--lsp` says when a name has several definitions), @pt-act (#397: pattern-screen hardening) and @liziye627-design (#431: a clone-gate test arm fix). Reports that led to fixes: @hnipps (#228, Django and unittest hooks reported as dead code) and @s0undt3ch (#305, duplicated test helpers).

## Versions and caches
Parser version 259, cache version 46, quality-snapshot scheme 24; the legend dictionary is `dictv=05b48ed93c807ee2 entries=981`. Caches written by 0.6.8 or any earlier build are rebuilt once.

Full notes: [CHANGELOG.md, section 0.6.9](https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/blob/v0.6.9/CHANGELOG.md).

name: v15.6.0
body:
## My Work: one store for the viewer's state (#5187)

My Work used to keep its state in three places: a hand-rolled module store, component state in `App`, and React contexts. It now runs on one Zustand store split into four slices: work, view, rules and focus.

**What you'll notice**
- **Reload and Back/Forward work.** The page, focus area and open request drawer are in the URL (`?view=`, `?focus=`, `?request=`).
- **Your list view, filter and sort are remembered** between visits. The theme still follows your system or `?theme=`. If browser storage is blocked, preferences last for the current visit only.
- **Live updates are steadier.** A stopped source can't publish. An older read never overwrites a newer live model. When a live update overtakes a save, you see the current model and your save is kept. Heartbeats re-render only the status indicators.
- **The drawer follows its request** by id and closes when the request leaves the feed. If the first read fails, you get a Retry button. A selected Closed filter stays visible even when nothing matches.
- **My Rules:** one save at a time, with controls disabled while a save runs. Each Approve/Reject receipt is tied to the version the worker saved, and Undo is refused once the rule has changed since.
- **My Focus:** all screens share one save history.

**Worker**
- Rule saves return `savedRuleId`.
- "Load in Claude Code" publishes the change to other open tabs.
- The feed signature includes `rulesFile`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v15.5.0...v15.6.0

name: MinerU 4.1.3
body:
中文

* Router 动态节点管理：支持运行时注册、查看和注销远程节点，通过独立管理密钥控制访问，无需重启即可调整节点池。
* 节点平滑退出：注销节点后停止分配新任务，等待已有任务、请求、下载及结果保留引用释放后再移除。
* API 过期时间精度：内部保留亚秒级时间精度，避免短保留期因整秒取整而提前失效；公开时间戳保持整数格式。
* 请求与运行时稳定性：修复重复文件传输可能触发的连接重置，改善反向代理路径前缀与 Unicode URL 兼容性，并优化空闲模型运行时的退出清理。
* 文档与集成示例：整理用户文档和历史资料，增加旧链接重定向与站点检查，补充 Tasks API、Router 管理、curl 和 n8n 示例。


English

* Dynamic Router upstreams: Register, inspect, and deregister remote workers at runtime using an independent management key.
* Graceful worker draining: Deregistered workers stop receiving new tasks and remain available until existing tasks, requests, downloads, and retained resource references are released.
* Precise API expiration: Preserve subsecond precision internally to prevent short retention periods from expiring early, while keeping public timestamps as integers.
* Request and runtime stability: Fix connection resets during duplicate file transfers, improve reverse-proxy path prefix and Unicode URL handling, and refine idle model runtime cleanup.
* Documentation and integration examples: Reorganize current and historical documentation, add redirects and site checks, and expand Tasks API, Router management, curl, and n8n examples.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/compare/mineru-4.1.2-released...mineru-4.1.3-released

name: MinerU 4.1.2
body:
## 中文

- **硬件诊断效率与输出**：`mineru-kit hardware info` 并行执行隔离的运行时探测，文本报告按固定顺序逐节输出并刷新；统一容量显示，精简设备与运行时摘要，JSON 保留完整诊断信息并补充 ONNX 只读候选设备及原因。
- **CLI 帮助按需加载**：根帮助、硬件帮助和版本查询不再初始化运行环境或读取用户配置，仅在实际执行命令时加载对应入口。
- **问题反馈表单**：提供独立的中英文表单，精简必填信息，解析档位默认选中“未知”；发布后自动同步最近五个稳定版本供选择。
- **CI 与发布流程**：问题表单变更使用轻量检查，发布重跑仍执行完整测试，避免被后续分支提交取消。

## English

- **Hardware diagnostics and output:** `mineru-kit hardware info` runs isolated runtime probes concurrently and flushes text sections in a fixed order as they become available. Capacity formatting and device summaries are clearer, while JSON retains full diagnostics and adds the read-only ONNX device candidate and selection reason.
- **On-demand CLI help:** Root help, hardware help, and version queries no longer initialize the runtime or read user configuration. Command entry points load only when executed.
- **Issue reporting:** Separate English and Chinese forms require less information, default the parsing tier to “Unknown,” and automatically offer the five most recent stable versions after each release.
- **CI and release workflows:** Issue-form changes use lightweight checks, while release reruns retain the full test suite and are protected from cancellation by later branch pushes.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/compare/mineru-4.1.1-released...mineru-4.1.2-released

name: MinerU 4.1.1
body:
## 中文

- **简化自动档位推荐**：移除推荐流程中的显存检测与容量门槛，直接复用小模型后端实际选择的 CPU/GPU 设备。选中 GPU 时开放全部四档，默认使用 Standard，Advanced 需要显式指定；选中 CPU 时，按进程可用逻辑核数推荐：不足 4 核仅开放 Flash，4–11 核开放到 Basic，至少 12 核开放到 Standard。
- **统一 llama.cpp 运行策略**：Linux 和 Windows 自动模式复用小模型后端的 CPU/GPU 选择，具体显卡由 llama.cpp 选择。这些平台上的 GPU 主模型默认使用 4 个生成线程，保留用户显式设置。
- **改善 PDF 文本清理**：在后置 OCR 和失败恢复完成后，将原生正文中残留的 Unicode 私用区字符替换为空格，减少异常字体映射造成的乱码，覆盖基本和补充私用区。

## English

- **Simplified automatic tier recommendations:** Remove GPU memory detection and capacity thresholds from tier recommendations, reusing the CPU/GPU device actually selected by the small-model backend. GPU selection enables all four tiers, with Standard as the default and Advanced available by explicit request. CPU selection uses the logical cores available to the process: fewer than 4 enables Flash only, 4–11 enables up to Basic, and 12 or more enables up to Standard.
- **Unified llama.cpp runtime policy:** Automatic mode on Linux and Windows reuses the small-model backend's CPU/GPU selection and lets llama.cpp choose the specific GPU. On these platforms, GPU models default to 4 generation threads while preserving explicit user settings.
- **Improved PDF text cleanup:** Replace residual Unicode private-use characters in native body text with spaces after post-OCR processing and fallback restoration, reducing garbled text caused by unusual font mappings. Both basic and supplementary private-use areas are covered.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/compare/mineru-4.1.0-released...mineru-4.1.1-released

name: v1.4.245
body:
## A faster Orca, plugins & background computer use ⚡

- ⚡ **A faster Orca:** Launch smoothly with hundreds of chats, with less lag as you type and switch tabs.
- 🧩 **Customize Orca** with icon themes, syntax highlighting and custom editors.
- 🖱️ **Keep working** while agents use Chrome, Blender and other Mac apps in the background.
- 🎙️ **Dictate on your phone** and see your words as you speak.
- 💬 **Try the new Chat UI:** Search for “Chat UI” in Settings to turn it on, then right-click a tab to switch live between Chat UI and TUI.

## Highlights

- **A faster Orca:** Fast app with hundreds of chats. Typing stays more responsive, and hidden chats do less work while you use other tabs.
- **Plugins:** Add icon themes, syntax highlighting and custom editors from Settings → Plugins. Community publishing is coming soon, so you’ll be able to share your own plugins.
- **Background computer use on Mac:** Let agents work in Chrome, Blender and other apps while you keep using your mouse and keyboard. Orca’s in-app browser already works in the background; now computer use does too. Some actions still need the app brought forward.
- **Chats:** Enjoy a very polished Chat UI, send again after Stop, and preview links in chat. Search for “Chat UI” in Settings to turn it on, and right-click a tab to switch live between Chat UI and TUI.
- **Terminals:** Set a running terminal limit for each computer in Settings → Terminal → Advanced.
- **WSL:** Stopped distros stay stopped until you choose Start. Terminals remember their folder.
- **Browser:** Press Cmd+Opt+B on Mac for a browser split. Send shorter annotation feedback, now with pasted images.
- **Workspaces:** Your workspace name becomes its branch name again. Source Control actions get Model and Effort controls.
- **Phone:** See dictation as you speak, and read clearer code, tables and diagrams.

## Compatibility & upgrade notes

- **New terminal host:** This release starts a fresh terminal host for new terminals. Terminals already open before the update keep running on the previous host and stay attached. The new running terminal limit setting needs the new host, and so do fixes such as the ble.sh startup fix and lighter process checks on macOS. Those apply to terminals you open after updating.
- **Plugins are on by default:** Installing a plugin, including from an `orca://plugins` link, only opens a review screen first. Plugins that run code ask for your consent before they install, and once approved they run with full access to your computer.
- **Running terminal limit:** The default now follows each computer: half of its system terminal limit, up to 4096, or 256 as before when Orca can’t read that limit. A value you set in Settings or with an environment variable takes priority. Raising or lowering it never closes running terminals. A remote server running an older Orca keeps working, but the limit can’t be changed there until it updates.
- **Chat naming:** Chats are now named by their own agent and account by default. A naming agent, custom command or arguments you saved before keep working, and the naming agent choice moved under Advanced in Settings → Chat → Chat naming.
- **Codex history across accounts:** A new switch, Settings → Agents → Share Codex history across accounts, is on by default and keeps today’s behavior. With it on, history from Orca’s managed accounts now also shows up in your own ~/.codex when you switch back to system default. Turning it off stops new sharing and removes nothing. On an SSH or WSL host running an older Orca, the switch stays disabled until that host updates.
- **Codex on macOS and Linux:** Orca now starts Codex with its paste guess turned off, so prompts typed from a phone or another client send instead of staying in the composer. Real pastes still arrive as pastes.
- **Computer use on a Mac:** Agents now act in the background by default. Agents can still ask for the old foreground mode with `--restore-window`, which drags into Chromium and Electron apps still need.
- **Browser annotations:** Send and Copy now give agents a short summary per note. Check **Include page details** in the Send menu to get the old full output; the choice lasts for that browser pane.
- **Workspace branch names:** A name you type for a new workspace is used as its branch again, even when Auto-rename branch from work is on. Auto-rename only replaces names Orca made up.
- **Automations:** Agents started by an automation skip their CLI’s startup update prompt, so the prompt can’t swallow the task. Agents you start yourself are unchanged.
- **Source Control actions:** Model and effort flags saved in an action’s Arguments move into the new Model and Effort controls when Orca loads; other Arguments stay as they are. A phone or remote server on an older Orca may launch these actions with a different model or effort until it updates.
- **New shortcuts:** Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+X opens Plugins (outside text fields), and Cmd+Opt+B on macOS opens a browser tab in a split to the right. Cmd+Opt+B can be changed in Settings → Keyboard.
- **Known limitation, downgrading:** If you go back to v1.4.244, custom model and effort choices on Source Control AI actions reset to the agent’s defaults, and updating again won’t bring them back.

---

## Product experience

### Native chat

*No more startup freeze with many chats, link previews, naming with the chat’s own agent, and a working Send after Stop.*

* Show chats as Interrupted or Done at startup without reading their history, so Orca no longer freezes after launch with hundreds of chats by @brennanb2025 in https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/32146
* Show hover cards for GitHub PR and issue links in chats by @AmoabaKelvin in https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/35199
